cross_references.notes: ECDC (2 Jun, citing DRC MoH) is the most recent primary figure at 321 DRC confirmed + 48 deaths; WHO DON605 (29 May) shows 134 confirmed total (DRC+Uganda) and 18 confirmed deaths, consistent with the rapid trajectory; Uganda count grew from 9 (29 May, WHO) to 15 (2 Jun, ECDC/Uganda MoH); Germany case (1, stable) confirmed by WHO and CDC; suspected-case counts vary significantly due to DRC MoH harmonisation removing ruled-out cases on 29 May, so the 116 under investigation figure (ECDC) is the most current post-harmonisation denominator for suspected cases.

locations.name: Mongbwalu Health Zone
locations.notes: Original epicentre where WHO received first alert on 5 May; MSF is constructing a 65-bed Ebola Treatment Centre here; 20 confirmed per WHO DON605 sitrep of 27 May.

locations.name: Rwampara Health Zone
locations.notes: Initial INRB confirmations came from Rwampara samples; 33 confirmed cases per WHO DON605 27 May sitrep; one of the highest-burden health zones.

locations.name: Bunia Health Zone
locations.notes: Capital of Ituri Province and largest confirmed case cluster (37 per WHO 27 May); WHO DG Tedros visited here 30–31 May; refurbished Ebola Treatment Centre with 24 beds opened.

locations.name: Nyankunde Health Zone
locations.notes: 10 confirmed cases reported per WHO DON605 sitrep; cases identified after 18 May expansion; among four highest-burden Ituri health zones.

locations.name: Ituri Province (other 11 health zones)
locations.notes: Aggregated confirmed cases across 11 additional Ituri health zones beyond Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu and Nyankunde; Ituri total is 299 confirmed across 15 health zones per ECDC 2 June.

locations.name: Goma
locations.notes: First Nord-Kivu confirmed case on 17 May; a woman who travelled from Ituri; city under M23/AFC rebel governance, limiting access for response teams; high cross-border mobility with Rwanda.

locations.name: Butembo
locations.notes: Cases identified 18 May; former epicentre of the 2018–2020 Zaire Ebola epidemic; under M23/AFC rebel governance with no functional Ebola-response infrastructure.

locations.name: Nord-Kivu Province (other health zones)
locations.notes: 19 confirmed cases across 7 health zones in Nord-Kivu per ECDC 2 June report; ADF and M23 presence complicates contact tracing and response access.

locations.name: Sud-Kivu Province (Miti Murheza / Kabare HZ)
locations.notes: First Sud-Kivu case confirmed 21 May in Miti Murheza health zone, Kabare territory; 3 confirmed across 1 health zone per ECDC 2 June; under rebel governance with severely limited response capacity.

locations.name: Kampala
locations.notes: 15 confirmed cases in Uganda as of 2 June per ECDC; 8 of 9 with known location are in Kampala; at least 7 associated with local transmission and 4 with direct DRC travel links; Uganda has closed borders with DRC.

locations.name: Fort Portal
locations.notes: Ugandans who attended a burial in eastern DRC on 18 May returned and were taken to Fort Portal for treatment after developing symptoms; case count included in Uganda total.

locations.name: Charité Hospital Berlin
locations.notes: US physician (Peter Stafford) who worked in DRC tested positive 17–18 May; evacuated to Charité 19 May; in stable condition as of 2 June; high-risk contacts transferred to Germany and Czech Republic and remain asymptomatic.

timeline.event: Red Cross announces (23 May) that three Red Cross workers who died 5–16 May are believed to have contracted BDBV on ~27 March during dead-body management activities in Mongbwalu — pushing likely outbreak start back by ~7 weeks.
Estimated date of first suspected death in the outbreak per WHO experts; virus believed to have circulated undetected for approximately 2 months before formal confirmation.
Index case — a nurse — presents with fever, hemorrhage, vomiting and malaise at a medical centre in Bunia, Ituri Province, DRC; later dies. (WHO DON602 / DRC MoH)

Suspected index case — a nurse at Evangelical Medical Centre, Bunia — develops fever, bleeding, and severe weakness; dies within days. Retrospective investigation suggests she was infected by a patient, implying community transmission was already ongoing.
Earliest known suspected case — a healthcare worker in Bunia — reports symptom onset (fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting); dies at Bunia medical centre. (WHO DON602)
Index case: healthcare worker in Bunia develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and intense malaise — first known suspected case of the outbreak, later dies at a Bunia medical centre.

Suspected index case — a healthcare worker in Bunia, Ituri Province — develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting, and intense malaise; the individual subsequently dies. This is the earliest known suspected case.

First known suspected case: a healthcare worker in Bunia HZ develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting, and intense malaise; the individual subsequently dies. First confirmed index of symptomatic disease.
First known suspected case — a healthcare worker in Bunia, Ituri Province — develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and malaise; later dies at a medical centre in Bunia. (WHO DON602)
Earliest known suspected case: health worker in Bunia, Ituri Province, develops fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting and malaise; dies ~27 April.

First confirmed death: a health worker in Bunia, Ituri Province, develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting and malaise; body repatriated to Mongbwalu mining zone for burial, triggering super-spreader funeral event.
Earliest known suspected case: health worker in Bunia, Ituri, develops fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting, and malaise; later dies at a medical centre in Bunia (WHO DON602).
First currently known suspected case — a health worker — reported symptom onset (fever, hemorrhaging, vomiting) per WHO DON602; died at Bunia medical centre.
Index case: a health worker in Ituri reports symptom onset (fever, haemorrhage, vomiting, malaise) and dies at a medical centre in Bunia — earliest known suspected case per WHO DON602.

Retrospective index case: health worker in Bunia presents with fever, haemorrhaging, vomiting, intense malaise; dies at Bunia medical centre — earliest known suspected case of the 2026 outbreak (WHO DON602).
Second case reported in Ituri; samples sent to Kinshasa — test methodology defaults to Zaire ebolavirus Xpert assay, returning false-negative results; outbreak continues undetected.
Cluster of unexplained haemorrhagic fever deaths flagged in Mongbwalu, Ituri Province, DRC.
WHO alerted to a high-mortality outbreak of unknown etiology in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including deaths of four health workers within four days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including deaths among healthcare workers; initial GeneXpert tests in Bunia return negative for Zaire Ebola.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness cluster in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 healthcare worker deaths within 4 days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality cluster of unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including 4 health-worker deaths within 4 days.
WHO alerted to unknown illness with high mortality in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, including four healthcare worker deaths within four days.
WHO alerted to a high-mortality outbreak of unknown illness in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri Province, including deaths among four healthcare workers within four days.
WHO alerted to unknown illness with high mortality in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including 4 healthcare worker deaths within 4 days. (WHO DON602)
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri, including four health worker deaths within four days.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness cluster in Mongbwalu Health Zone including 4 health-worker deaths; rapid response team dispatched to Ituri.
WHO alerted to unknown high-mortality illness in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri, including reports of 4 healthcare workers dead within 4 days; rapid response team dispatched.

WHO alerted to high-mortality outbreak of unknown illness including HCW deaths in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri; initial Xpert tests negative for Ebola-Zaire — 10-day diagnostic delay begins due to BDBV-specific genomic divergence (~30%) from Zaire ebolavirus.
WHO alerted to high-mortality outbreak of unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, DRC, including deaths among health workers.
WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including 4 HCW deaths within 4 days; initial Xpert tests negative (do not detect BDBV).

WHO alerted to high-mortality unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including deaths of 4 health workers within 4 days. First known suspected case onset retrospectively dated to 24 April 2026.

WHO receives alert about unknown high-mortality illness in Mongbwalu HZ, Ituri; four healthcare workers dead within four days; initial Xpert tests negative (false negatives due to ~30% BDBV/ZEBOV genetic divergence).

WHO alerted to high-mortality outbreak of unknown illness in Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri, including deaths among health workers. First known suspected case (nurse) had onset of symptoms 24 April and died in Bunia. MSF receives alerts of suspected viral haemorrhagic fever from early May; ~55 deaths since beginning of April documented.
MSF receives alerts of increased hemorrhagic fever deaths in Mongbwalu; team deployed finds 55 deaths since early April. (MSF statement)
59-year-old Congolese man admitted to Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, Uganda with severe symptoms; later confirmed as first imported BVD case in Uganda. (Africa CDC / Uganda MoH)
Elderly Congolese man admitted to Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, Uganda, with severe Ebola-compatible symptoms (later confirmed BDBV-positive on 15 May).
First Uganda case (59-year-old Congolese man) admitted to Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, with severe symptoms; died 14 May.
Rapid-response teams investigate Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZs; 13 blood samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa for advanced analysis. (WHO DON602)
WHO rapid-response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones. (WHO DON602)
WHO/DRC rapid-response teams conduct in-depth field investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara Health Zones; samples collected and sent to INRB Kinshasa.
WHO rapid response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones; 13 blood samples from Rwampara sent to INRB Kinshasa for analysis.
WHO/DRC rapid response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara health zones; samples sent to INRB Kinshasa. (WHO DON602)
Rapid response teams complete in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZ; initial Xpert Ebola tests on 20 samples return negative because assay targets Zaire ebolavirus only.
WHO rapid response team conducts in-depth investigation in Mongbwalu and Rwampara HZs; 20 samples collected, initially test negative using standard Ebola Xpert (Zaire-only assay).
INRB Kinshasa analyses samples; PCR confirms Orthoebolavirus in 8 of 13 specimens; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). (WHO DON602 / INRB)
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 confirmed Orthoebolavirus-positive by PCR on 15 May. Second Uganda imported case confirmed in Kampala on 16 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara; 8 test positive by PCR for Orthoebolavirus. (WHO DON602)
INRB analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR; results released 15 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples; standard Xpert tests in Bunia earlier returned false negatives for all 20 samples tested, as the test detects only Zaire ebolavirus.
INRB Kinshasa receives 13 blood samples from Rwampara HZ for analysis; initial field Xpert tests had been negative for Zaire ebolavirus, causing a ~3-week diagnostic delay.
Initial Xpert tests on 20 Rwampara samples at Bunia Provincial Public Health Lab return false-negative for Ebola virus; samples forwarded to INRB. (WHO DON602)
First Kampala case dies. INRB analyses 13 samples from Rwampara HZ.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 samples from Rwampara Health Zone; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR. Genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) on 15 May.
INRB Kinshasa analyses 13 blood samples from Rwampara HZ; 8 test positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR on 15 May; genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV).
INRB Kinshasa analyzed 13 blood samples from Rwampara HZ; 8 confirmed positive for BDBV on 15 May by PCR; genomic sequencing confirmed Bundibugyo virus species.
INRB confirms 8/13 samples positive for Bundibugyo virus; genomic sequencing confirms species. First Uganda case death. Second Uganda case confirmed 16 May.
Bundibugyo virus confirmed by laboratory (8 of 13 samples positive). First confirmed case detected in Kampala, Uganda.

DRC Ministry of Public Health officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak; Uganda MoH confirms imported BVD case — 59-year-old Congolese male who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala, on 2026-05-14. (DRC MoH / Uganda MoH / Africa CDC)
Africa CDC activates Incident Management Support Team; convenes urgent cross-border coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan, WHO and partners. (Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak; INRB confirms 8 positive samples by PCR, genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case — a 59-year-old Congolese man who died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala.

INRB genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (died 14 May in Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call. (WHO DON602; Africa CDC)

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC; genomic sequencing confirms Bundibugyo virus (BDBV/Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense). Uganda MoH simultaneously declares outbreak following first confirmed imported case in Kampala (Kibuli Muslim Hospital). Africa CDC convenes urgent high-level regional coordination meeting with DRC, Uganda, South Sudan and 130+ global partners.

INRB confirms 8 of 13 samples positive for Orthoebolavirus by PCR; genomic sequencing identifies Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). DRC MoH officially declares the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (Kampala). Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination statement: ~246 suspected cases, 65 deaths.

INRB confirms Bundibugyo virus in 8 of 13 samples. DRC MoH officially declares DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported BVD case (59-year-old Congolese male who died 14 May in Kampala). Africa CDC alerts continent and convenes emergency regional coordination meeting with 130+ participants.

INRB confirms Bundibugyo virus (Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense) by PCR in 8 of 13 samples; DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (Kampala death). Africa CDC issues continental alert. (WHO DON602 / DRC MoH / Africa CDC)

INRB confirms Bundibugyo virus in 8 of 13 samples by PCR; genomic sequencing confirms BDBV species. DRC MoH declares 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case. Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call.

DRC Ministry of Public Health officially declares DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak; 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths across Rwampara, Mongbwalu, and Bunia. Uganda MoH concurrently confirms first imported BVD case (59-yr-old Congolese male, died 14 May, Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala).
Africa CDC issues continental alert; CDC issues Level 3 Travel Health Notice for DRC and Level 1 for Uganda; 65 contacts listed in DRC, 15 classified high-risk.
DRC Ministry of Health officially declares the country's 17th Ebola outbreak (2nd BDBV) in Rwampara, Mongbwalu, and Bunia HZs. Uganda MoH simultaneously confirms imported BDBV case in Kampala.

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC. Uganda MoH confirms first imported BDBV case (Kampala). INRB confirms BDBV in 8/13 samples from Rwampara HZ. Africa CDC issues continental alert. CDC issues Level 3 (DRC) and Level 1 (Uganda) travel health notices.
DRC MoH officially declared the 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirmed first imported case. Africa CDC issued regional alert. CDC issued Level 3 (DRC) and Level 1 (Uganda) Travel Health Notices.

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak; Uganda MoH confirms first imported BVD case (death 14 May); CDC issues Level 3 DRC and Level 1 Uganda travel health notices; Africa CDC alerts continent to regional spread risk.

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak. Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (Congolese male, died 14 May, Kibuli Hospital, Kampala). Africa CDC alerts continent and calls urgent regional meeting.

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak; Uganda MoH confirms first imported case (Kampala); INRB confirms Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense by PCR and genomic sequencing; Africa CDC issues continental alert.
DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo, Ituri Province); INRB confirms BDBV by PCR and genomic sequencing; Uganda MoH simultaneously confirms first imported case in Kampala.

DRC MoH officially declares 17th Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo virus, Ituri Province). Uganda MoH confirms imported case — 59-year-old Congolese male died at Kibuli Muslim Hospital, Kampala (onset 11 May, died 14 May). INRB confirms 8/13 samples positive for BDBV. Africa CDC issues urgent regional coordination call.
Second confirmed Kampala case (fatal). Suspected Kinshasa case reported (later retracted).
Second imported confirmed case identified in Kampala with no apparent link to the first; suspected Kinshasa case tests negative on confirmatory INRB PCR and is disconfirmed. (WHO PHEIC / INRB)
WHO Director-General determines the Bundibugyo outbreak in DRC and Uganda constitutes a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC); does not meet pandemic emergency criteria. (WHO)

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC for Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC and Uganda; determination cites 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in Ituri plus 2 confirmed cases in Kampala and 4 HCW deaths. Africa CDC holds 130-participant high-level consultative meeting.

Second imported case confirmed in Kampala (unlinked to first). WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC. 246 suspected cases, 80 suspected deaths in Ituri confirmed at this time-point. (WHO PHEIC declaration)

Second unrelated confirmed case reported in Kampala, Uganda. WHO Director-General declares a PHEIC under IHR Article 12 — without convening an Emergency Committee, citing the gravity of the situation. Africa CDC activates its Incident Management Support Team.

WHO Director-General determines outbreak constitutes a PHEIC (declared without Emergency Committee, a first in WHO history). Second imported case confirmed in Kampala. Kinshasa alert issued; later retracted after confirmatory INRB testing negative.

WHO Director-General Tedros declares PHEIC without convening an Emergency Committee — a historic first. Second unlinked imported case confirmed in Kampala. Suspected Kinshasa case ruled out by INRB confirmatory testing. Africa CDC convenes high-level meeting including DRC, Uganda, South Sudan and donors.

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC — first ever without convening Emergency Committee first; second imported case confirmed in Kampala; as of this date: 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in DRC. (WHO PHEIC Notice)

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC. Second imported Kampala case confirmed. WHO reports 8 lab-confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 deaths in Ituri. Kinshasa suspect tests negative on confirmatory INRB testing.

Second independent imported case confirmed in Kampala (no link to first case). WHO Director-General declares PHEIC — not pandemic emergency — under IHR Article 12. Africa CDC convenes high-level regional coordination meeting with 130+ participants.
WHO Director-General declares PHEIC (not pandemic emergency) for BDBV in DRC and Uganda. Second confirmed case reported in Kampala. Kinshasa suspect case tests negative (retracted).

WHO DG declares PHEIC for Ebola-BDBV in DRC and Uganda — 8th PHEIC under IHR (2005). As of this date: 8 confirmed, 246 suspected, 80 suspected deaths in Ituri; 2 confirmed imported cases in Kampala. Africa CDC convenes high-level consultative meeting with 130+ participants from affected and donor countries.

Second imported Uganda case confirmed in Kampala (no link to first). WHO DG declared PHEIC under IHR Article 12 — first-ever PHEIC declared before convening Emergency Committee. DRC reported 246 suspected cases and 80 deaths.
INRB/INSP confirms outbreak; second Uganda Kampala case (unlinked) confirmed; WHO formally announces PHEIC under IHR; Africa CDC convenes 130-participant high-level regional coordination meeting.
WHO Director-General declares Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC).

INRB/AFP confirms Goma case: wife of a Bunia Ebola fatality tested positive after traveling to Goma (North Kivu) while already infected, extending geographic spread beyond Ituri. (INRB via AFP / Al Jazeera)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Bundibugyo virus disease; CDC and US State Dept coordinate medical evacuation to Germany for treatment; 6 additional high-risk contacts also moved to Germany. (CDC / NBC News)

An American healthcare worker in DRC tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo; US officials coordinate evacuation of seven individuals to Germany for care. CDC confirms Level 2 travel health notice for DRC, Level 1 for Uganda.
WHO Emergency Committee to be convened; WHO Director-General confirms PHEIC declared without prior Emergency Committee recommendation — a first in WHO history, citing extraordinary urgency.
WHO formally announces PHEIC; does not declare pandemic emergency. INRB confirms first case in Goma (North Kivu) — wife of Bunia fatality. (WHO; INRB via AFP)
US missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia; CDC confirms an American has tested positive. (Serge charity; CDC briefing)

INRB Director Muyembe confirms laboratory-positive case in Goma, North Kivu (M23-held city of >1 million, on Rwandan border). Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. Rwanda closes Goma–Gisenyi border crossings indefinitely. American missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; CDC confirms first US national infected.

First confirmed case in Goma, North Kivu, reported — a woman who travelled from Ituri. Africa CDC raises figures to 336 suspected cases, 88 deaths, 13 confirmed. INRB director Muyembe confirms spread to North Kivu.

American physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; CDC confirms the first US national infected. Six other Americans classified as high-risk exposures; all to be moved to Germany for treatment and monitoring.

Confirmed case in Goma (North Kivu) announced by INRB Director Prof. Muyembe — wife of Bunia Ebola death who travelled to Goma while already infected. CDC confirms outbreak now affects at least 9 health zones in Ituri. US CDC triggers enhanced travel monitoring for DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan.

Confirmed case in Goma, North Kivu (wife of Bunia Ebola victim) reported by INRB director Prof. Muyembe to AFP; CDC transcript confirms 9 health zones affected in Ituri. (Al Jazeera / AFP / CDC Transcript)

American physician Dr. Peter Stafford (medical missionary, Serge organization) tests positive for Ebola Bundibugyo disease in Ituri; CDC begins coordination for medical evacuation to Germany. (CDC Situation Summary)
Goma (North Kivu) case confirmed: wife of a Bunia Ebola death travelled to Goma while infectious. Outbreak now spans Ituri and North Kivu provinces.
American physician Dr. Peter Stafford (Serge/CTSM missionary at Nyankunde Hospital, Bunia) tests positive for BDBV — first confirmed American case in this outbreak.

First confirmed case in Goma (North Kivu) — wife of Bunia fatality who travelled while infected. Rwanda closes DRC border. CDC holds first public media briefing on outbreak; 9 health zones now affected in DRC.
US physician Dr. Peter Stafford tests positive for BVD at Bunia hospital (confirmed 18 May); CDC and State Dept arrange medical evacuation of Stafford plus 6 high-risk contacts to Germany.
Confirmed BDBV case reported in Goma, Nord-Kivu. Outbreak now spans Ituri and Nord-Kivu. CDC issues Level 3 Travel Health Notice for DRC (reconsider nonessential travel), Level 1 for Uganda.
American surgeon Dr. Peter Stafford (Serge mission, Nyankunde Hospital, Bunia) tests positive for BDBV after unknowingly operating on an Ebola patient pre-outbreak confirmation.
Case confirmed in Goma, Nord-Kivu. Kinshasa suspected case retracted after INRB confirmatory test returned negative.
Confirmed case in Goma, Nord-Kivu (M23-controlled). Kinshasa suspected case ruled out by INRB. ECDC threat assessment brief published. Hong Kong activated Ebola preparedness plan.

WHO Director-General declares PHEIC — first-ever PHEIC declared by a DG before convening an Emergency Committee, invoking urgency provisions of IHR Article 12; Goma first North Kivu case confirmed same day.

WHO DG declares PHEIC — first ever PHEIC declared before Emergency Committee convened. CDC issues Level 3 (DRC) and Level 1 (Uganda) travel notices. American healthcare worker tests positive (exposure in DRC, 17 May).
WHO DG declares PHEIC — first-ever PHEIC declared without prior Emergency Committee convening; first Goma (Nord-Kivu) case confirmed.
WHO DG declares PHEIC — eighth-ever under IHR (2005); determination: 'PHEIC but does not meet pandemic emergency criteria'; DRC confirmed cases at 8; DRC+Uganda combined 10 confirmed deaths.

WHO DG declares PHEIC — Bundibugyo virus disease in DRC and Uganda constitutes a PHEIC but not a pandemic emergency under IHR. First confirmed case in Goma (Nord-Kivu). WHO stresses no approved vaccines or therapeutics for BDBV.
Outbreak expands from 3 to 9+ health zones in DRC. New confirmed case in Goma (under M23 rebel control). US CDC enacts enhanced travel screening.
Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); reports ~395 suspected cases and 106 associated deaths across DRC and Uganda. (Africa CDC)

CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening, Title 42 entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who traveled to DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the prior 21 days; CDC EOC activated. (CDC / DHS)

CDC Situation Summary (most recent official update) reports 11 confirmed cases and 336 suspected cases including 88 deaths in DRC, and 2 confirmed cases including 1 death in Uganda across 9 health zones. (CDC Situation Summary)

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS); 395 suspected cases and 106 deaths confirmed. US CDC/DHS invoke Title 42, restricting entry of non-US passport holders who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in prior 21 days.

Ebola confirmed in Goma, North Kivu (rebel-held M23 city); Rwanda closes Goma-Gisenyi border crossings. Confirmed case also reported in Beni, North Kivu. DRC Health Minister announces three new Ebola treatment centres opening in Ituri.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3(F) of Africa CDC Statute. 395 suspected cases, 106 associated deaths reported. (Africa CDC PHECS declaration)

CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 travel restrictions; entry restrictions placed on non-US passport holders from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan in previous 21 days. CDC moves 7 Americans (1 confirmed case + 6 high-risk contacts) to Germany for care. (CDC)
CDC current situation page confirms 9 health zones in Ituri Province now affected; EU announces PPE stockpiles ready for deployment and detection kit support to Africa CDC. (CDC; CNN)

Africa CDC formally declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC and DHS invoke Title 42 for at least 30 days restricting entry of non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda or South Sudan within the previous 21 days. US moves 7 people (1 confirmed case, 6 high-risk contacts) from DRC to Germany for treatment/monitoring. US Embassy in Uganda temporarily suspends visa services. DRC Health Minister announces opening of 3 new Ebola treatment centres in affected region. WFP airlifts >5 tonnes of medical supplies to Ituri. OCHA reports 482 suspected cases and ~116 deaths in Ituri province alone.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3, Paragraph F of the Africa CDC Statute. CDC and DHS implement enhanced US travel screening and Title 42 entry restrictions for travellers from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan within 21 days. CDC confirms 9 health zones in Ituri affected. US State Department issues Do Not Travel advisory for DRC and South Sudan; Reconsider Travel for Uganda and Rwanda.

Africa CDC declares PHECS. American Christian missionary physician Dr. Peter Stafford confirmed positive for Bundibugyo virus in Bunia; US working to evacuate 7 Americans (1 positive, 6 high-risk) to Germany. CDC + DHS invoke Title 42 restricting entry of non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, South Sudan (21-day rule). Confirmed cases in Butembo (North Kivu) reported by WHO representative. DRC begins establishing field hospitals in Bunia. Total at CDC: 10 confirmed, 336 suspected, 88 deaths in DRC; 2 confirmed incl. 1 death Uganda.

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) under Article 3F; ~395 suspected cases and 106 deaths reported at time of declaration. US CDC and DHS implement Title 42 entry restrictions on non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda and South Sudan. (Africa CDC PHECS / CDC)
DRC authorities begin establishing field hospitals in Bunia after city hospitals overwhelmed; DRC health minister announces 3 Ebola treatment centres to be opened. (Wikipedia / PBS)

Africa CDC declares outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS invoke Title 42 entry restrictions: 30-day ban on non-US nationals who visited DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in preceding 21 days. CDC confirms 9 health zones affected in Ituri. CDC reports 10 confirmed, 336 suspected, 88 deaths (DRC) + 2 confirmed, 1 death (Uganda).

Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS invoke Title 42 — 30-day entry restriction for non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within prior 21 days. DRC opens field hospitals in Bunia after existing facilities overwhelmed.
Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS implement US Title 42 entry restrictions for non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan.

Cases identified in Butembo (Nord-Kivu) and Nyakunde (Ituri), bringing affected health zones to 11 (DRC) per CDC 20 May update. Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). CDC/DHS invoke Title 42 entry restrictions: 30-day ban on non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the preceding 21 days.
American physician Peter Stafford confirmed positive for Bundibugyo virus disease on 17–18 May; first American case in the 2026 outbreak.

Cases identified in Butembo (Nord-Kivu) and Nyakunde (Ituri). Africa CDC declared Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS). American missionary Peter Stafford confirmed positive in DRC. CDC/DHS implemented Title 42 travel restrictions and entry measures for DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. Fort Portal Uganda cluster (burial attendees) identified.

CDC and DHS issue 30-day prohibition on non-US nationals who have been in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan in the prior 21 days; enhanced screening for returning Americans; Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security.
Cases confirmed in Butembo (Nord-Kivu) and Nyakunde (Ituri); field hospitals established in Bunia after city hospitals overwhelmed; ECDC deploys EU Health Task Force expert to Africa CDC HQ.

Africa CDC officially declares PHECS. CDC and DHS announce enhanced US travel screening, entry restrictions on non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan; Dulles Airport routing for affected travellers.
Cases confirmed in Butembo (Nord-Kivu) and Nyakunde HZ (Ituri); CDC/DHS implement enhanced US entry restrictions and traveler screening for DRC, Uganda, South Sudan.

CDC and DHS announce enhanced travel screening and 21-day entry restrictions on non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan; affected passengers rerouted to four US airports (IAD, ATL, IAH, JFK).

Africa CDC declares Public Health Emergency of Continental Security. Cases identified in Butembo (Nord-Kivu). US physician tests positive for Ebola. Uganda reports 2 HCWs among cases. ECDC Threat Assessment Brief published.

OCHA reports 482+ suspected cases since April in Ituri; confirms Goma case; warns hostile environment (insecurity, displacement, hunger) is severely hampering response; >5 tonnes of supplies airlifted to Ituri by WFP.
UN News and NBC report outbreak approaching ~500 suspected cases and 116 associated deaths; case in Beni (North Kivu) also reported; situation remains rapidly evolving.

OCHA and UN partners warn hostile environment in eastern DRC is severely hampering response; nearly 10 million people in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu face crisis-level hunger compounding outbreak risk. ECDC deploys expert to Africa CDC headquarters. Reuters witnesses Congolese nationals turned back at Bukavu-Rwanda border. Outbreak total now exceeds 482 suspected cases across at least 9 health zones per OCHA.

DRC daily health bulletin reports 516 suspected cases, 33 confirmed cases, and 131 deaths — including 26 new deaths in 24 hours. WHO representative Dr Anne Ancia confirms spread to North Kivu (Goma and Butembo). Butembo records first 2 confirmed cases (INRB). WHO technical advisory group convenes to assess vaccine options, including Ervebo (Merck) cross-protection potential; WHO notes 2-month timeline before any vaccine could be deployed.

CDC situation page updated: 536 suspected + 105 probable + 34 confirmed + 134 deaths across DRC and Uganda (2 confirmed + 1 death Uganda included). Ugandans who attended a burial in eastern DRC and returned home develop symptoms; some transferred to Fort Portal for treatment. Uganda bans handshakes, hugs, and unnecessary physical contact. Germany confirms arrangements to receive American patient.

Confirmed cases reported in Butembo (North Kivu) by WHO field rep Dr. Ancia (UN News); Fort Portal, Uganda cases identified among Ugandans who attended DRC burial. CDC MoH figures: 536 suspected + 105 probable + 34 confirmed + 134 deaths. US State Dept issues Level 4 Do Not Travel for DRC, Uganda, South Sudan; commits $23M + funding for up to 50 treatment clinics. (CDC/State Dept/UN News)
Uganda government temporarily bans handshakes, hugs and unnecessary physical contact. (Wikipedia/AP)
Dr. Peter Stafford (American) safely evacuated from DRC to Germany for treatment; 6 high-risk American contacts also evacuated to Germany. (CDC / UPI / Serge)

Dr. Stafford airlifted to Charité Hospital, Berlin, Germany — first Ebola medical evacuation to Europe in this outbreak. Six high-risk US contacts evacuated to Germany and Czech Republic. Uganda bans handshakes, hugs, and unnecessary physical contact. DRC MoH reports ~500+ suspected, 131 deaths.

WHO DG Tedros expresses 'serious concern' over 'scale and speed' of epidemic at WHO Director-General briefing; DRC reports 513 suspected cases and 131 deaths. Dr. Stafford transported to Germany. Uganda bans handshakes, hugs, and unnecessary physical contact. UN News confirms cases in Butembo.

Chinese researchers publish multivalent mRNA vaccine study targeting EBOV, BDBV, and SUDV in PNAS; vaccine is pre-clinical (animal studies only). WHO vaccine official confirms two BDBV vaccine candidates under agency review.

Dr. Peter Stafford evacuated to Charité University Hospital, Berlin, Germany for treatment; wife Dr. Rebekah Stafford and 4 children evacuated to same hospital for monitoring. Dr. Patrick LaRochelle (potential exposure) sent to Bulovka Hospital, Prague.

WHO representative Dr. Anne Ancia confirms confirmed cases in both Butembo and Goma, Nord-Kivu; warns outbreak could take two months before a vaccine is available and recalls the 2018–2020 two-year response.

CDC confirms American physician Peter Stafford (missionary, Nyankunde Hospital) in transit to Berlin Charité hospital for treatment; 6 high-risk contacts moved to Germany and Czech Republic for monitoring.

American patient (Peter Stafford) evacuated from DRC to Germany for treatment; high-risk contacts moved to Germany and Czech Republic. WHO Emergency Committee met; confirmed PHEIC, ruled out pandemic emergency. WHO released USD 3.9M from Contingency Fund for Emergencies; OCHA allocated USD 60M.

WHO IHR Emergency Committee convened (first meeting); Uganda government temporarily bans handshakes and unnecessary physical contact; Uganda postpones Martyrs' Day celebration (potential 2-million-person gathering).

American missionary physician Peter Stafford, who tested positive on 17 May at Nyankunde Hospital near Bunia, airlifted to Berlin Charité hospital; high-risk contacts moved to Germany and Czech Republic for monitoring.

First meeting of WHO IHR Emergency Committee convened; outbreak confirmed in Nord-Kivu (Goma). American healthcare worker evacuated to Germany for treatment; high-risk contacts moved to Germany and Czech Republic.
American physician Peter Stafford airlifted from DRC to Charité Hospital Berlin; 6 high-risk contacts moved to Germany and Czech Republic for monitoring.

US physician Peter Stafford medically evacuated from DRC to Charité Hospital Berlin; first Ebola medevac to Europe in current outbreak; Uganda temporarily bans handshakes and unnecessary physical contact.

US physician (Peter Stafford) evacuated to Charité Hospital Berlin for treatment; CDC and DHS announce enhanced US travel screening, entry restrictions for non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan; flights rerouted to 4 designated US airports. Uganda bans handshakes and physical contact.

WHO DG addresses World Health Assembly and media: 51 confirmed in DRC (Ituri and North Kivu), 2 confirmed in Uganda; ~600 suspected cases and 139 suspected deaths; Emergency Committee convened and agrees event is PHEIC but not pandemic emergency. (WHO DG Briefing 20 May 2026)

WHO reports ~600 suspected cases (51 confirmed) and 139 deaths in DRC + 2 confirmed (1 death) in Uganda. WHO DG warns of 'scale and speed' concern. Butembo cases confirmed in North Kivu. Ugandans who attended DRC burial taken to Fort Portal for treatment. Person in Ontario, Canada, tested for Ebola as precaution (result pending). White House reported to have resisted Dr. Stafford's return to US.

WHO Emergency Committee meets in Geneva; Tedros confirms ~600 suspected cases and 139 suspected deaths — largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever by factor >4x. Outbreak confirmed in 11 health zones across Ituri and Nord-Kivu. Ugandans who attended DRC burial develop symptoms; some taken to Fort Portal.

Person returning to Ontario, Canada from East Africa tested for Ebola as precautionary measure; result pending. US flights from DRC/Uganda/South Sudan redirected to Washington-Dulles for enhanced public health screening.
WHO Director-General Tedros confirms at press briefing: ~600 suspected cases, 139 suspected deaths, 51 confirmed in DRC, 2 imported in Uganda; PHEIC reaffirmed but not upgraded to pandemic emergency.
Group of Ugandans who attended a burial in eastern DRC return to Uganda with Ebola symptoms; taken to Fort Portal for treatment and isolation.
Person who returned to Ontario, Canada from East Africa tested for Ebola as a precautionary measure; result reported as negative (no confirmed case).

WHO DG Tedros confirms to media: ~600 suspected cases, 139 suspected deaths; 51 confirmed cases in DRC (Ituri and Nord-Kivu); PHEIC status maintained; outbreak risk assessed as high nationally and regionally, low globally.

WHO DG press briefing: ~600 suspected cases, 139 suspected deaths, 51 DRC confirmed + 2 Uganda confirmed + 1 American (Germany). DRC MoH epidemiological update: 13 new confirmed cases (12 Ituri, 1 Nord-Kivu). Over 1,000 contacts followed in Ituri. Uganda Martyrs' Day celebrations (up to 2 million attendees) postponed by President Museveni.

WHO DG briefing confirms 600 suspected cases, 139 suspected deaths, 51 confirmed DRC + 2 Uganda; DRC MoH epidemiological update reports 13 new confirmed cases since 19 May (12 Ituri, 1 Nord-Kivu). Over 1,000 contacts under follow-up in Ituri.

ECDC updates situation assessment (18:00 CET): confirms ~600 suspected cases and 139 deaths per WHO as of 20 May; Bahrain and other countries announce 30-day entry suspensions for travellers from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan; Asian governments bolster border screening.

DHS orders all US-bound flights carrying passengers present in DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan within past 21 days to land at Washington-Dulles for enhanced health screening. Air France flight diverted to Montreal after DRC traveller boarded in error.

CDC/DRC-Uganda MoH report: 575 suspected cases, 51 confirmed, 148 deaths across 11 health zones. Dr. Stafford reports being 'cautiously optimistic' from Berlin hospital. White House denies Washington Post report of initial US refusal to allow repatriation.

First Ebola case confirmed in South Kivu Province by AFC/M23 rebel alliance (rural area near Bukavu); patient was a 28-yr-old man who travelled from Kisangani, Tshopo Province, hundreds of km from Ituri epicentre; UN separately confirms a second South Kivu case (woman contact of Beni travellers). Protests erupt in Rwampara over disputed Ebola death; police fire warning shots; two treatment tents burned.
All returning US citizens/residents from DRC, Uganda, or South Sudan required to enter the US exclusively via Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) for health screening.
India–African Union announce postponement of India-Africa Forum Summit (originally 28–31 May, New Delhi) citing 'emerging public health situation in Africa' — direct reference to Ebola outbreak.

South Kivu (Bukavu) case confirmed — patient who transited through Tshopo Province; spread to 3rd DRC province. Rwampara protests: police used tear gas after community members burned patient treatment tents. India-Africa Forum Summit postponed. US Dulles-only routing for returning Americans from DRC/Uganda/South Sudan.

Sud-Kivu province first case confirmed: 28-year-old died near Bukavu after transiting from Kisangani, Tshopo Province — a major river hub not previously in the outbreak footprint, signalling undetected transmission chain.

Community resistance in Rwampara: residents protested a disputed burial; police fired warning shots and tear gas; protestors burned two treatment tents; attack complicates IPC and community engagement.
India-Africa Forum Summit (New Delhi, 28–31 May) postponed due to Ebola; Uganda suspends all public passenger transport to DRC for 4 weeks.

Confirmed case in Sud-Kivu Province reported (3rd DRC province), linked to Tshopo Province transit. India-Africa Forum Summit postponed. Uganda suspends public transport to DRC. WHO DG media briefing cites ~750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.
South Kivu (Bukavu) first case confirmed – patient reportedly travelled from Kisangani (Tshopo Province), extending confirmed geographic spread to 3 DRC provinces.

Reuters/CNBC Africa reports WHO Africa regional director warns against underestimating Bundibugyo risk; DRC MoH May 21 bulletin: 670 suspected cases, 61 confirmed, 160 suspected deaths — highest figures to date.

WHO IHR Emergency Committee issued temporary recommendations. WHO DG revised risk assessment: very high at national level, high at regional level, low at global level. DRC: ~82 confirmed, 7 confirmed deaths; ~750 suspected, 177 suspected deaths. Uganda: 2 confirmed, 1 death, no onward transmission. WHO/Africa CDC establishing continental Incident Management Support Team.

WHO DG upgrades DRC national risk to 'very high'; ~750 suspected cases, 177 suspected deaths, 82 confirmed DRC cases with 7 confirmed deaths + 2 Uganda confirmed + 1 death reported at media briefing. First confirmed case in Sud-Kivu (new province) also announced.

WHO IHR Emergency Committee temporary recommendations published: both DRC and Uganda directed to declare national/sub-national health emergencies; candidate therapeutics noted under consideration for clinical trials; fast-tracking of candidate vaccine evaluation underway.

CDC transcript briefing: 7 additional HQ subject matter experts on VHF to be deployed to DRC and Uganda; exit screening (assessment + temperature) ongoing in DRC and Uganda; ~25 CDC staff in DRC country office.

WHO DG Member State session: WHO CFE releases $3.9 million; UN OCHA allocates $60 million to response; WHO + Africa CDC establishing continental Incident Management Support Team; multi-agency SPRP to be published imminently.

WHO IHR Emergency Committee issues temporary recommendations; WHO risk assessment upgraded to 'very high' for DRC and 'high' for Uganda. EU Health Security Committee issues common EU approach opinion including exit-screening guidance.
WHO IHR Emergency Committee issues temporary recommendations to State Parties; WHO upgrades DRC national risk to 'very high'; US extends entry restrictions to green card holders.
WHO upgrades DRC outbreak risk to 'very high' at national level, 'high' at regional level, 'low' at global level; IHR Emergency Committee issues temporary recommendations to State Parties.

WHO IHR Emergency Committee issues temporary recommendations to States Parties. WHO upgrades DRC risk to 'very high' national, 'high' regional, 'low' global. IPC temporary recommendations published 22 May.

Uganda MoH announces 3 new confirmed cases (total now 5), including a driver who transported the first patient, a health worker, and a DRC woman who travelled Arua–Entebbe–Kampala; CDC confirms same. WHO DG calls for 'high vigilance'.

Ugandan authorities confirm first local transmissions: a driver and a healthcare worker exposed to the index Kampala patient test positive; Uganda temporarily bans handshakes and unnecessary physical contact.
Two further healthcare workers at a private hospital in Kampala test positive for BVD, bringing Uganda total to 7 at that point; DRC confirmed cases exceed 100.
Uganda confirms two additional healthcare worker cases in Kampala, bringing Uganda total to 7 as of 27 May; NICD South Africa reports no cases in South Africa.
Oxford Vaccine Group announces ChAdOx1 BDBV candidate vaccine being fast-tracked with Serum Institute of India; could enter clinical trials within 2–3 months pending animal-study data.
NICD SitRep: DRC MoH reports 1,077 suspected cases including 246 deaths; Uganda total 7 confirmed including 2 healthcare workers and 1 death as of 27 May.

Uganda closes DRC borders for at least four weeks; 21-day isolation required for DRC entrants. Uganda has 7 confirmed cases (2 HCWs added 25 May) and 1 death. NICD: 121 DRC confirmed, 17 confirmed deaths including 4 HCWs, 1,077 suspected.

WHO convenes Technical Advisory Groups on therapeutics and vaccines. Prioritises MBP134, Maftivimab (Regeneron), and remdesivir for clinical trials; obeldesivir for post-exposure prophylaxis. PARTNERS trial reactivated in DRC and Uganda.

Wikipedia/Reliefweb aggregate: ~1,262 suspected+confirmed cases and at least 241 deaths reported (pre-recount peak); Africa CDC reports pledged international donor funds ($500M) fell sharply within days.

WHO DON605: 134 confirmed (incl. 9 Uganda) with 18 confirmed deaths as of 29 May; DRC MoH revises suspected-case count downward after removing ruled-out cases; Germany's US patient counted separately.

WHO DON605 published: 134 confirmed (incl. 9 Uganda), 18 confirmed deaths, 906 suspected, 223 suspected deaths as of 27–29 May. DRC MoH harmonises suspect case count, removing ruled-out cases; CDC notes revised lower suspected total.

International Rescue Committee warns outbreak is 'likely significantly larger than official figures suggest' with only 20% of contacts being traced; MSF states 'response has not yet caught up to the rapid spread.'

WHO DG Tedros arrives in Bunia, Ituri; meets DRC PM Judith Suminwa Tuluka in Kinshasa, then flies to epicentre. Makes direct appeal to armed groups to declare ceasefire. IRC warns outbreak 'likely significantly larger' than official figures with only ~20% of contacts traced.
DRC MoH publishes revised figures: 282 confirmed cases, 42 confirmed deaths, 220 suspected cases under investigation (after removing ruled-out cases and pending-investigation deaths on 29 May).
WHO backs three experimental therapeutics (MBP134, maftivimab/Regeneron, remdesivir) and obeldesivir for PEP for formal evaluation in clinical trials; PARTNERS trial reactivated in DRC and Uganda.

WHO DG Tedros visits Bunia, opens new Ebola treatment centre; honours five recovered healthcare worker survivors (4 nurses, 1 lab worker); Africa CDC DG Kaseya writes FT op-ed citing 263 confirmed, 43 deaths, >1,100 suspected cases.
DRC MoH publishes updated harmonised figures: 282 DRC confirmed cases, 42 confirmed deaths, 220 suspected cases under investigation; Ituri: 264 confirmed (14 HZs), Nord-Kivu: 15, Sud-Kivu: 3.

WHO DG Tedros opens refurbished Ebola Treatment Centre in Bunia (24 beds, expandable to 60+42). WHO/DRC joint statement reaffirms partnership. MSF issues 'deeply alarming' statement: 'Never before has an Ebola outbreak recorded so many cases so soon after its declaration.'

ECDC updates threat assessment confirming 282 DRC confirmed + 9 Uganda confirmed (291 total); WHO DG Tedros visits Bunia epicentre; 5 health workers reported recovered per UN News; outbreak described as 'evolving rapidly' with ongoing cross-border transmission.

CEPI announces up to $62M to fast-track three Bundibugyo vaccine candidates (IAVI rVSV-BDBV, Moderna mRNA, Oxford/Serum Institute), the first-ever dedicated BDBV vaccine funding at scale; no licensed vaccine exists.
Brazil rules out Ebola in two patients (Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo) who had returned from DRC/Uganda; Italy also rules out one suspected case; no confirmed cases outside DRC, Uganda, and Germany.
DRC government data (per AP) shows outbreak has spread to 22 health zones across three eastern provinces, up from 17 previously; Africa CDC reports 1,100+ suspected cases and 246 suspected deaths.

WHO announces four nurses discharged from Bunia ETC after recovering from Ebola; five total recoveries to date. UN News reports 16 healthcare workers infected in DRC. China sends specialist team to DRC. CEPI commits up to $62M to fast-track three BDBV vaccine candidates (IAVI rVSV, Moderna mRNA, Oxford/SII ChAdOx1).

ECDC updates tracker (2 Jun): DRC MoH reports 321 confirmed cases, 48 confirmed deaths, 116 suspected under investigation; Uganda reports 15 confirmed cases and 1 death. Brazil and Italy rule out Ebola in previously suspected cases. Total confirmed: 337 across DRC, Uganda, Germany.

alerts.title: PHEIC Declared — Bundibugyo Virus Disease, DRC & Uganda
alerts.body: WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May 2026. As of 2 June, 321 confirmed cases and 48 deaths in DRC, 15 confirmed and 1 death in Uganda, 1 confirmed in Germany — 337 total. No approved vaccine or therapeutic exists for Bundibugyo virus. ECDC reports 23 health zones now affected across 3 DRC provinces.

alerts.title: Africa CDC: Public Health Emergency of Continental Security
alerts.body: Africa CDC declared a PHECS on 18 May 2026 and has identified nine additional at-risk African countries (Angola, Burundi, CAR, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania, Zambia). The outbreak spans three DRC provinces and has crossed into Uganda and Germany.

alerts.title: No Approved Vaccine or Therapeutic for Bundibugyo Virus
alerts.body: Unlike Zaire Ebola, no licensed vaccine or treatment exists for BDBV. WHO has prioritised MBP134, maftivimab, and remdesivir for clinical trials, and obeldesivir for post-exposure prophylaxis. CEPI committed up to $62M on 1 June for three candidate vaccines — none yet in clinical trials.

alerts.title: Healthcare Worker Infections: 16 Infected in DRC, 4 Confirmed Deaths
alerts.body: As of 1 June, 16 healthcare workers have contracted Ebola in DRC. Four confirmed HCW deaths were reported by 27 May. WHO characterised this as 'a disease you get when you care for someone,' highlighting severe IPC gaps.

alerts.title: MSF: Response Has Not Caught Up — 'Deeply Alarming'
alerts.body: MSF warned on 30 May 2026 that this outbreak has recorded more cases sooner after declaration than any previous Ebola outbreak. Only ~20% of contacts are being traced. Hundreds of samples remain untested. The IRC warns the true scale is likely significantly larger than official figures.

alerts.title: Armed Conflict Obstructing Response in Nord-Kivu and Ituri
alerts.body: ADF fighters and ethnic militias have attacked health teams in Ituri. M23/AFC controls Goma and Butembo in Nord-Kivu — the highest-risk nodes for regional spread — with no functional Ebola infrastructure. Uganda and Rwanda have closed DRC borders. Tedros appealed to armed groups for a ceasefire on 28 May.

alerts.title: Brazil and Italy Rule Out Ebola in Suspected Cases
alerts.body: São Paulo ruled out Ebola in a DRC returnee (meningitis confirmed) and Rio de Janeiro ruled out Ebola in a Uganda traveller (malaria confirmed, negative saliva/urine Ebola tests on 1 June). Italy also ruled out one suspected case. No confirmed Ebola cases outside Africa and Germany as of 2 June 2026.

alerts.title: US Travel Restrictions: DRC, Uganda, South Sudan
alerts.body: CDC has imposed 21-day entry restrictions on non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. Air passengers are rerouted to four designated US airports (IAD, ATL, IAH, JFK). As of 2 June, no confirmed Ebola cases in the United States.

news.title: Brazil and Italy Rule Out Ebola in Suspected Cases Amid DRC Outbreak
news.summary: Brazil ruled out Ebola in two patients in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro tested after travel to DRC and Uganda. Italy similarly ruled out a suspected case, providing temporary relief from concerns about Americas-bound spread.

news.title: ECDC: DRC Reports 321 Confirmed Ebola Cases, Uganda Now Has 15 Confirmed
news.summary: The ECDC outbreak tracker updated 2 June citing the DRC MoH: 321 confirmed cases and 48 deaths in DRC, with 299 from 15 Ituri health zones, 19 from 7 Nord-Kivu zones, and 3 from 1 Sud-Kivu zone. Uganda's confirmed count rose to 15, with at least 7 cases linked to local transmission.

news.title: CEPI Commits Up to $62M to Fast-Track Three Bundibugyo Vaccine Candidates
news.summary: CEPI announced on 1 June 2026 fast-track funding of up to $62M for three investigational BDBV vaccines: up to $3.2M for IAVI's rVSV platform, up to $50M for Moderna's mRNA candidate, and up to $8.6M for Oxford/Serum Institute's ChAdOx1 candidate. None are yet in clinical trials.

news.title: Four Nurses Discharged After Recovering from Ebola in DRC — Five Total Survivors
news.summary: WHO announced on 1 June that four nurses at the Bunia Ebola Treatment Centre were discharged after recovery, adding to a laboratory worker cleared the previous Thursday — five total recoveries. WHO stressed early care is lifesaving even without approved therapeutics.

news.title: China Sends Specialist Team to DRC to Assist Ebola Response
news.summary: China's Foreign Ministry announced on 1 June 2026 that it had dispatched a team of specialists to DRC to support the Ebola outbreak response, adding to growing international assistance alongside US, EU, and regional commitments.

news.title: WHO Chief Tedros Opens New Ebola Treatment Centre in Bunia, Hails Five Recoveries
news.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros visited Bunia on 30–31 May, opening a refurbished 24-bed ETC (expandable to 102 beds) and announcing five patient recoveries. He appealed to armed groups for a ceasefire and pledged WHO's continued commitment to the DRC response.

news.title: MSF: Ebola Spreading 'Faster Than Any Previous Outbreak' — Response 'Not Caught Up'
news.summary: MSF warned on 30 May that this is 'the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak ever recorded,' with hundreds of samples untested and response constrained by border closures, conflict, and logistics failures. Only ~20% of contacts are being traced, says the IRC.

news.title: WHO Expert Advisory Prioritises MBP134, Remdesivir, Obeldesivir for BDBV Trials
news.summary: WHO's Technical Advisory Group recommended MBP134 and maftivimab antibodies plus remdesivir for confirmed-case clinical trials, and oral obeldesivir for post-exposure prophylaxis. The PARTNERS trial has been reactivated in DRC and Uganda pending regulatory approval.

news.title: Nature: Clinical Trials for Bundibugyo Treatments 'In a Strong Position' to Launch Quickly
news.summary: Nature reports that trials for MBP134 (Mapp Biopharmaceuticals) and remdesivir already have DRC ethics board approval and are awaiting regulatory sign-off. MBP134 showed protection in primates even at advanced illness stages, including against Bundibugyo virus specifically.

news.title: CNN Frontline Report: Doctors Work Around the Clock in Ituri's Overwhelmed Hospitals
news.summary: CNN gained extraordinary access to the Ebola epicentre in Ituri Province, documenting overstretched health workers, fear among communities, and fragile hope as DRC's healthcare system struggles to contain the rapidly spreading Bundibugyo virus.

news.title: WHO Ebola Outbreak Collides with Conflict and Hunger in Eastern DRC — Tedros Warns
news.summary: WHO warned that conflict, poor roads, and insecurity are blocking aid in affected areas where nearly 10 million people face acute hunger. Tedros said health facilities are 'either non-functional or operating under severe constraints' due to insecurity across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, and Sud-Kivu.

news.title: Science: Race to Launch Fast Clinical Trials Against New Ebola Outbreak Faces Major Hurdles
news.summary: Science reports that while trial protocols for remdesivir and MBP134 have ethics approval in DRC, researchers face severe obstacles: mistrust of health care systems, armed conflict, more treatment centres and diagnostics needed, and no Bundibugyo vaccines ready for parallel prevention trials.

background.virus: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV); formal species name Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense
background.discovery: 2007, during an outbreak in Bundibugyo District, Uganda; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel species distinct from Zaire ebolavirus by ~30% genetic divergence — the same divergence that caused false-negative Xpert tests in 2026, delaying detection by ~10 days
background.case_fatality_rate_historical: 25–50% (WHO: 30–50%; CDC: ~25–50%; 2007–08 Uganda: 25–32%; 2012 DRC: ~34%); confirmed-case CFR in 2026 outbreak is ~15% (49 deaths / 337 confirmed as of 2 Jun), lower than historical precedent, likely reflecting surveillance expansion into milder cases and improving supportive care, but denominator uncertainty remains significant given ongoing reclassification
background.transmission: Direct contact with blood, body fluids, or tissues of infected people or animals; contact with contaminated surfaces, fomites, or bodies of deceased individuals. Individuals are infectious only when symptomatic. Funeral and burial practices are a key transmission amplifier. Fruit bats are the suspected zoonotic reservoir. Does not spread via air or casual contact.
background.symptoms: Sudden fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat — followed by vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, rash, impaired kidney/liver function, internal and external bleeding; nosebleeds and vomiting blood reported in current outbreak. Co-infection with malaria should be considered in differential diagnosis.
background.vaccines_therapeutics: No approved vaccine/therapeutic for BDBV; CEPI commits $62M (1 Jun) for IAVI rVSV-BDBV, Moderna mRNA, Oxford/SII ChAdOx1; WHO prioritises MBP134, maftivimab, remdesivir for clinical trials; obeldesivir for post-exposure prophylaxis

past_outbreaks.notes: First identified outbreak; led to discovery and naming of the Bundibugyo strain; genomic sequencing confirmed a novel Orthoebolavirus species distinct from Zaire ebolavirus; WHO AFRO cites 131 cases and 42 deaths (CFR 32%) in some records.
Second documented Bundibugyo outbreak; contained within months in a remote area; final BDBV outbreak prior to 2026.

Second-largest Ebola outbreak in history, different species (Zaire ebolavirus), same geographic zone; Butembo was epicentre, now re-affected in 2026; response took over two years and is directly relevant precedent for current containment difficulties.

past_outbreaks.location: Bulape/Mweka Health Zones, Kasai Province, DRC (Ebola-Zaire)
past_outbreaks.notes: DRC's 16th Ebola outbreak declared 4 September 2025; declared over 1 December 2025 with 53 confirmed, 11 probable, and 45 deaths per CDC; immediately preceded the current 2026 BDBV outbreak — DRC's second Ebola outbreak within six months.

past_outbreaks.location: Ituri Province (15 HZs incl. Mongbwalu, Rwampara, Bunia), Nord-Kivu (7 HZs incl. Goma, Butembo), Sud-Kivu (1 HZ) — DRC; Kampala / Fort Portal — Uganda; Berlin (medical evacuation) — Germany
past_outbreaks.cfr: ~15% confirmed-case CFR (49 deaths / 337 confirmed per DRC MoH/ECDC as of 2 Jun 2026); crude CFR undetermined given ongoing reclassification; ~116 suspected under investigation post-harmonisation
past_outbreaks.notes: Third and largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded by factor >2× the previous largest (149 cases, 2007–08); PHEIC declared WHO 17 May 2026; Africa CDC PHECS declared 18 May 2026; 321 confirmed DRC + 15 Uganda + 1 Germany = 337 total across 3 countries and 23 health zones as of 2 June 2026; no approved vaccine or therapeutic; CEPI commits $62M for three vaccine candidates on 1 June 2026.

why_this_matters: As of 2 June 2026, DRC MoH reports 321 confirmed cases and 48 confirmed deaths (per ECDC citing DRC MoH); Uganda has 15 confirmed cases and 1 death (7+ associated with local transmission); Germany has 1 confirmed (US physician, stable medical evacuation) — already the largest Bundibugyo outbreak ever recorded, with cases spread across at least 23 health zones in three DRC provinces. The outbreak has more than doubled in confirmed cases in the week since the previous data point (134 confirmed on 29 May).

No approved vaccines or therapeutics exist for Bundibugyo virus; licensed Ebola products (Ervebo/rVSV-ZEBOV; Zabdeno+Mvabea; Inmazeb; Ebanga) target Zaire ebolavirus only. CEPI committed up to $62M on 1 June 2026 for three candidate vaccines (IAVI rVSV-BDBV, Moderna mRNA, Oxford/SII ChAdOx1) — none yet in clinical trials. WHO has prioritised MBP134, maftivimab, and remdesivir for clinical trials with ethics approval already granted in DRC; obeldesivir is prioritised for post-exposure prophylaxis trials.

Uganda has confirmed 15 cases (as of 2 June) with at least 7 linked to local transmission events in Kampala — not just imported cases — and has closed its border with DRC. Fort Portal has also seen cases among Ugandans who attended a DRC burial on 18 May. The situation signals established cross-border transmission chains in a country with significant Ebola response experience but no BDBV-specific tools.

The outbreak spans three DRC provinces: Ituri (299 confirmed, 15 HZs — epicentre), Nord-Kivu (19 confirmed, 7 HZs including Goma and Butembo under M23/AFC rebel governance), and Sud-Kivu (3 confirmed, 1 HZ). M23/AFC-controlled cities represent the highest-risk nodes for regional and international spread due to rebel governance with no functional Ebola-response infrastructure and intense cross-border mobility.

Contact tracing remains critically insufficient at approximately 20% of contacts per the IRC (1 June). MSF states 'never before has an Ebola outbreak recorded so many cases so soon after its declaration' and warns the response 'has not yet caught up to the rapid spread.' Hundreds of samples remain untested. Approximately 3,600 contacts are being monitored in DRC. With 16 healthcare workers infected and 4 confirmed HCW deaths, IPC gaps are severe.

International spread risk is real but contained: Brazil and Italy both ruled out suspected Ebola cases by 2 June (meningitis and malaria confirmed respectively); the US physician in Germany is stable; no confirmed Ebola cases exist outside Africa and Germany. The US has imposed 21-day entry restrictions on non-US nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan; air passengers are rerouted to four designated US airports. Rwanda and Uganda have closed DRC borders.

DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan adopted a joint $319M response plan; the US pledged over $112M; China sent a specialist team (1 June); CEPI committed $62M for vaccines. Africa CDC has identified 9 at-risk neighbouring countries. WHO DG Tedros personally visited the epicentre (30–31 May), opening a new ETC in Bunia and appealing to armed groups for ceasefire.

With response depending entirely on classic public health containment — contact tracing, isolation, safe burials, community engagement — in an active conflict zone where ADF and M23 armed groups obstruct aid, three attacks on health centres have been recorded, over 1.2 million people in Ituri province alone need humanitarian aid, and the virus was undetected for approximately 7 weeks before declaration, this represents the most challenging Bundibugyo response scenario in history.
